lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Make the résumé’s target role clearer and give the bakery role less space than the quantitative work.
items.because: For a quant-research application, the bakery role is less relevant than the research experience.

items.says: Keep dates, punctuation, and location formatting consistent throughout.
Check that the phone, email, and code link are current and clickable where appropriate.
Make the code link lead directly to a polished profile or relevant work.
items.because: It should not lead to a generic landing page.

items.says: Confirm that “candidate” is the university’s formal status.
Confirm that the expected completion date is still accurate.
items.because: It should be updated if the degree has been completed or the date has changed.

items.says: Clarify whether six is the total team or the number supervised per shift.
Give the scope or outcome of staying within the weekly labour budget.
items.because: It would make the budget claim stronger.

items.says: Use “labor” rather than “labour.”
items.because: A U.S. résumé should use U.S. spelling consistently.

items.says: Give the measurement period for the reduction from 12% to 7%.
items.because: It would make the reduction easier to assess and verify.

items.says: Explain what “unsold bread” means in this context.
items.because: It would make the reduction easier to assess and verify.

items.says: Define the measure behind “risk-adjusted returns.”
State the comparison point and evaluation period for the 35% improvement.
Clarify whether the 35% improvement restates the later Sharpe improvement.
items.because: The two results may describe the same work.

items.says: Qualify the claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: An absolute claim needs substantiation across the full pipeline.

items.says: Explain how the purging and embargo were implemented.
Make your individual contribution and the team’s subsequent use of the feature store clear.
Distinguish approval for a future allocation from an allocation actually deployed.
items.because: The bullet should not imply live results if there were none.

items.says: The best of 400 backtested Sharpe ratios is not a defensible expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the best configuration creates selection bias.

items.says: Reassess whether this bullet belongs on the résumé.
items.because: The 400-way search makes the selected result particularly vulnerable to selection bias.

items.says: Clarify how this result relates to the earlier 35% improvement and the Kaggle result.
items.because: The signal and Sharpe gains may describe the same work.

items.says: State the relevant benchmark and period clearly.
Explain how the 18-month out-of-sample period was kept separate from model or parameter selection.
items.because: The other backtest results may be affected by the same selection process.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker may invalidate the 2,000-run study.
items.because: Workers can generate repeated sequences rather than independent trials.

items.says: Clarify what computation was parallelized.
items.because: The current wording is repetitive.

items.says: Clarify what the comparison with the previous variance bound means.
Check that “under review at JASA” is still the accurate publication status.
Give the number of student responses or the source of the teaching rating, if available.
items.because: The rating is more interpretable with that context.

items.says: Identify how the 3,000 downloads were counted.
items.because: The figure could otherwise be ambiguous.

items.says: Make sure the R package is accessible from the code link.
Give more of the evaluation setup, including the forecast horizon and test period.
items.because: That would make the baseline comparison interpretable.

items.says: Check that the Holm correction covers the comparisons described.
Define the crisis periods if they are not obvious from the paper or linked materials.
Add meaningful competition context or results, or remove the bullet.
items.because: The current wording is too general to show your contribution or outcome.

items.says: Explain how you determined validation leakage was present.
items.because: Otherwise, the causal claim is hard to judge.

items.says: Explain what the 0.02 score gap represents.
items.because: Otherwise, the significance of the number is hard to judge.

items.says: Resolve the overlap with the Northpeak order-book signal result.
items.because: If it is the same signal or evaluation, it should not be counted as a separate achievement.

items.says: Remove Kafka or add evidence of practical experience with it if you cannot discuss that experience.
items.because: Kafka appears without support elsewhere in the résumé.

items.says: “Time-series econometircs” contains a typo.
